original_value: Gait phase detection is a new biometric method which is of great significance in gait correction, disease diagnosis, and exoskeleton assisted robots. Especially for the development of bone assisted robots, gait phase recognition is an indispensable key technology. In this study, the main characteristics of the gait phases were determined to identify each gait phase. A long short-term memory-deep neural network (LSTM-DNN) algorithm is proposed for gate detection. Compared with the traditional threshold algorithm and the LSTM, the proposed algorithm has higher detection accuracy for different walking speeds and different test subjects. During the identification process, the acceleration signals obtained from the acceleration sensors were normalized to ensure that the different features had the same scale. Principal components analysis (PCA) was used to reduce the data dimensionality and the processed data were used to create the input feature vector of the LSTM-DNN algorithm. Finally, the data set was classified using the Softmax classifier in the full connection layer. Different algorithms were applied to the gait phase detection of multiple male and female subjects. The experimental results showed that the gait-phase recognition accuracy and F-score of the LSTM-DNN algorithm are over 91.8% and 92%, respectively, which is better than the other three algorithms and also verifies the effectiveness of the LSTM-DNN algorithm in practice.

result.paraphrase: Gait phase detection is an emerging biometric technique with major importance for gait correction, disease diagnosis, and exoskeleton-assisted robots. In particular, for bone-assisted robot development, gait phase recognition is an essential key technology. In this study, the main features of gait phases were extracted to identify each phase. A long short-term memory deep neural network (LSTM-DNN) algorithm is proposed for gait detection. Compared with the conventional threshold method and LSTM, the proposed approach achieves higher detection accuracy across different walking speeds and different test subjects. In the recognition process, acceleration signals from accelerometer sensors were normalized so that the different features shared the same scale. Principal component analysis (PCA) was then used to reduce dimensionality, and the processed data were used to form the input feature vector for the LSTM-DNN algorithm. Finally, the dataset was classified with a Softmax classifier in the fully connected layer. Multiple male and female subjects were tested with different algorithms for gait phase detection. Experimental results showed that the LSTM-DNN algorithm achieved over 91.8% gait-phase recognition accuracy and over 92% F-score, outperforming the other three algorithms and confirming its practical effectiveness.
